**Session summary: brain — phase-0 epic re-sync (#402, PR #403)**

## Goal
Phase-0 bookkeeping of epic #313, after a full-scope architecture audit of `main` @ `5ef85df`: re-sync the docs that drifted from the shipped tree, clear the standing drift-guard, and close tickets already satisfied in code. Ref: issue #402, PR #403.

## What was done
- **`docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md` re-synced.** It still claimed the reviewer flow-guarantees were inert (#317) and that the release gate ran after the tag (#210) — both shipped. Also corrected GitLab parity (all 8 MR gates blocking since Q5 Phase 5; the residual is rung-2/rung-3, #130) and replaced the "un-ticketed" M4 prose with the new ticket refs.
- **`AGENTS.md` regenerated** from its 5 SOURCE_DOCS via the antigravity backend — the M3 merge changed `reviewer-protocol.md`, leaving the drift-guard red. Suite 2263/2264 → 2264/2264.
- Epic #313 body updated with a dated status block; #369 and #263 closed as satisfied-in-code; M4 hard gate decomposed into #396-#401.

## BUG FOUND — the engram transport drops `issue`, and it blocks #368 / T2.1
While capturing this very record scoped to issue #402, the standing REQ-C4-1 contract test went red: the record failed round-trip id-equality. Root cause, traced through the seam:

- `buildRecord` includes `issue` in the hashInput (per memory-format.md:67), so a scoped record hashes differently.
- `importRecord` (record -> engram observation) has **no home for `issue`** — the observation shape is `{type, project, title, content, created_at, scope}`.
- `exportObservation` therefore cannot restore it, so the recomputed id differs from the stored id (`rec-4e5cce32ee0b4047` vs the stored `rec-c0d159bba82a6a95`).

Consequence: **any record carrying `issue` fails REQ-C4-1 today.** This is the mechanical reason #368 sits at 0% adoption — populating the field is not merely unadopted, it is currently *impossible* without breaking the round-trip contract. Since T2.1 memory-gate promotion depends on issue-scoped records, this seam is on the critical path for that promotion. The record was therefore written WITHOUT `issue`, matching every other record in the store, and the defect filed separately.

This is a seam-blindness defect of exactly the class M10 (#335) exists to close: green suite, contract silently unsatisfiable in the one direction nobody exercised.

## Findings worth carrying forward
- **The epic body drifted from its own tickets.** A roadmap pass derived from it proposed #210 as "1.1 first item" — #210 is closed and shipped. A source-of-truth doc needs a re-sync ritual or it misdirects the next agent.
- **M3 core is merged but the milestone exit is not met.** `5ef85df` wired the refuter (via `lib/causal-admission.mjs`) and tier-activated `/2`, but there are still no inline per-line comments — the literal exit criterion. Residuals: #381 (findings do not round-trip: render emits a YAML list, parse reads a JSON scalar), #382 (self-review fail-open in code, masked by config), `follow_ups[]` wired but unreachable, `/2` undogfoodable while brain declares `tier: lite`.
- **M4 was the biggest tracking gap**: the epic hard gate lived only as prose. Now #396 (rollback/atomic), #397 (clobber asymmetry), #398 (downgrade ratchet), #399 (corrupt-JSON lockout), #400 (npx brain init), #401 (danger-path e2e — makes the gate checkable).
- **Recurring defect class**: "one rule, two implementations" — #315, #316, #340. Worth batching as one initiative with drift-guards.

## Decisions
- One PR for both files: same atomic cause (the M3 merge), 130 lines, splitting would double the gate ritual for docs-only changes.
- Record written without `issue` rather than shipping a store that fails its own contract test.
- No `status:approved` applied by the agent — that is the human keystroke per #124 doctrine.

**Session summary: brain — M3 post-merge defect cleanup (#381, #382) + roadmap re-sync**

## Goal
Continue Phase 1 after the M3 core merge (`5ef85df`, #394): fix the two known reviewer defects, close the M3 residual tracking gap, and re-sync epic #313 so the roadmap is derivable from tickets rather than prose.

## What shipped
- **#381 → PR #406 (`c881a04`).** `findings` and `follow_ups` now survive the `renderVerdict` → `parseVerdict` round trip. Root cause: `renderVerdict` emits a YAML block list, `parseVerdict` read it with `scalar()`, whose `^findings:[ \t]*(.+)$` requires same-line content. Only `findings: []` matched. `follow_ups` was rendered by M3 but never parsed by anything — write-only since it shipped.
- **#382 → PR #407 (`e67dff8`).** Self-review abstention now fails closed at boot when `reviewer.handle` is empty. The same missing handle also made the anti-loop guard inert (it compares `lastVerdict.author` against that handle), so one fix restored two guards. The fail-open was deliberate, not an oversight — a strict guard would have abstained from every review while the handle was unresolvable — but that premise expired with #367.

## Tickets filed (M3 residuals — the milestone exit is NOT met)
- **#409** — `regulated`-tier e2e. Recommended FIRST: it is the harness the other two need to prove anything.
- **#405** — inline per-line `comments[]`, GitHub+GitLab parity. Needs an ADR-0020 amendment and a Tier-2 promotion of `vcs-contract.md` before any code: no contract for it exists yet.
- **#408** — no evaluator emits `pre-existing`/`base-only`; `follow_ups[]` is unreachable and the refuter never fires.
- **#404** — engram transport drops `issue`; blocks #368 → T2.1 promotion.
- **#410** — this memory materialization.

## Epic #313 re-synced
Critical path **inverted deliberately**: M4 (#396–#401) is now the highest-priority track, with M3 closure in parallel. Rationale recorded in the body: M4 is the hard gate blocking external adopters *today*; M3 residuals block reviewer *completeness*. The two touch disjoint surfaces, so nothing serialises them. Added a cross-cutting section for #404 (it belongs to no milestone yet blocks #368 → T2.1) and a standing rule for future agents: work described only in prose in that body is a bug — file an issue for it.

## Process notes that cost time
- Worktree-per-issue is the repo's workflow (`AGENTS.md`, load-bearing). `brain:ticket:start --worktree` fails in Claude-Code-on-the-web (`VCS token not found in .env` — the container has the GitHub MCP server, not a `gh` token); reproduce the branch convention manually from `deriveBranchType` + the 40-char slug rule.
- Worktrees do not inherit `node_modules`; symlink it or nothing runs.
- A combined branch being green does not prove each split half is green — run the full suite per worktree. Baseline on `e67dff8` is 2268 tests.
- Commit signing is impossible in this container (0-byte `commit_signing_key.pub`, no private key, no `ssh-keygen`); merged history already carries unsigned Claude commits.
- Deleting remote branches is blocked by the git proxy; `fix/issue-381-382-reviewer-roundtrip` is orphaned and needs deleting via the GitHub UI.

**Defect class: render/parse asymmetry hidden by testing only the empty encoding (brain, #381)**

`renderVerdict` serialised `findings` as a YAML block list; `parseVerdict` deserialised it with a scalar regex requiring content on the same line. Every non-empty findings list was silently dropped on the round trip.

**The generalisable lesson is why the full suite stayed green.** The only encoding that round-tripped — `findings: []` — was the only encoding under test. Coverage over a serializer/parser pair proves nothing unless the tests exercise the *non-degenerate* shape.

Two practices adopted in the fix, worth repeating for any wire-format work in this repo:
1. Tests drive the real `buildVerdict` → `renderVerdict` pair and parse the actual output. Hand-written fixture strings encode the author's belief about the format, which is exactly the thing under doubt.
2. New tests were run against the OLD parser to confirm they fail (3 of 4 did). The 4th — the empty case — passes against both and was kept deliberately, as an in-repo record of the blind spot that hid the defect.

Related: this is the same "green in test, inert in production" class that M10 (#335) exists to close. It was found by reading the code, not by a failing test, which is itself evidence for #409 — brain runs the `lite` tier, so the whole `/2` path has no production exercise.

**M3 shipped consumers without producers — three wired-but-unreachable paths (brain)**

After the M3 core merge, three code paths exist, are correct, and can never execute in production:

1. **`follow_ups[]`** — `verdict.mjs:51` routes a `causal_disposition` of `pre-existing`/`base-only` into it, `schema-v2.mjs` admits both values, `reviewer-protocol.md:216,222` documents them. **No evaluator emits either.** `causal-admission.mjs:23` states why, correctly: none of the current checks compare against base closely enough to claim it honestly, and "inventing the claim would be worse than omitting it". The gap is that no check which *can* make the claim was ever built. Tracked in #408.
2. **The refuter** (`evaluators/refuter.mjs`, #284) — runs only when a blocker carries `evidence_class: 'inferential'`. No evaluator produces inferential findings, so it is a documented no-op, deliberately wired so a future producer needs no second integration point. Same ticket, #408.
3. **The entire `/2` tier** — activation routes `lite`/`standard` → `/1` and `regulated` → `/2`, and brain declares `lite` (ADR-0026, #358). Everything M3 built is covered by unit tests and by nothing else. Tracked in #409.

**Consequence to carry forward:** #381 made `follow_ups` *readable*, not *populated* — it moved from broken to empty, not to working. Do not read a green suite or a merged PR as evidence that this feature works end to end.

**Empirical evidence for #404, found while inspecting the store:** zero records across `2026-06.jsonl`, `2026-07.jsonl` and `2026-08.jsonl` carry an `issue` field. That is the "~0% adoption" #368 describes, and the cause is the transport dropping the field, not authors omitting it. Note `computeRecordId` DOES hash `issue` when present, so the format supports it — only the transport does not.

**Session summary: brain — #396 slice 1, restore-point rollback for brain:upgrade**

## Goal
Pick up the brain 1.1 line and advance M4 — the epic #313 hard gate that blocks external
adopters from upgrading safely. Owner chose M4 over M3 closure, then chose to deliver #396
as a two-slice chain.

## Accomplished
- **#396 slice 1 shipped to review** — PR #412 (draft), chain `main ← feature/issue-396-rollback
  ← PR #412 ← PR#2`. `copyManaged` now snapshots every path it may write before the first
  write and restores those bytes on any throw; an incomplete rollback KEEPS its snapshot and
  reports where. Symlinked managed paths are refused up front. Suite 2268 → 2282.
- **Full SDD change dir written** at `openspec/changes/issue-396-upgrade-rollback/` —
  proposal, spec (REQ-396-1..9 with scenarios and negative controls), design, tasks, plus
  `brain-drafts/adr-0027-upgrade-rollback-is-restorable-not-atomic.md`.
- **Three follow-up issues filed**: #413, #414, #415. Epic #313 re-synced with a status block,
  a rewritten M4, and an explicit priority table for the next agent.

## Discoveries
1. **#396's stated exit criterion is unachievable as written.** `rename(2)` is atomic for ONE
   path; the managed payload spans four disjoint locations (`brain/**`, `.github/**`,
   `.gemini/**`, root files), so no single directory swap can commit it. Multi-file atomicity
   needs a journal. Restated as *restorability*, with each residual gap named — ADR-0027 draft,
   unsigned.
2. **A signal handler cannot interrupt a synchronous fs loop.** Measured: SIGINT at 40ms into a
   935ms sync copy loop → the loop ran to completion (i=60000) and the handler fired after;
   the same loop with a `setImmediate` yield aborted at i=2251. So registering a handler is not
   a mid-write abort — it suppresses the default terminate action, which is the only thing that
   genuinely half-applies a tree. The real managed write is 366 files in ~23ms.
3. **`spawnSync` returns `{status: null, signal}` when the child dies by signal.** A first
   revision claimed, as measured, that a Ctrl-C during `npm install` was caught by the deferred
   interrupt guard. It was not: `if (r.status !== 0)` fires first, reporting the interrupt as
   "install failed — check repo access" and collapsing exit 130 into 1. Registering the handler
   is what kept the parent alive to reach that branch, so the slice introduced that regression.
   Fixed by testing `r.signal` before `r.status`. Recorded rather than rewritten out of history.
4. **`existsSync` follows symlinks.** A dangling symlink at a managed path therefore read as
   absent, was recorded as created-by-this-run, and was DELETED on rollback — while
   `copyFileSync` wrote through the link to a target outside the repo, and the rollback reported
   success. The feature corrupting what it exists to protect. Presence must be judged with
   `lstat`.
5. **A `finally` is the wrong place to discard a restore point.** It runs after `catch`, so it
   deleted the snapshot on the incomplete-rollback path — the one branch where the snapshot is
   the only surviving copy of the consumer's bytes, and the same branch whose message tells the
   operator to go inspect them. Only a complete rollback may discard.
6. **Annotating a caught error can throw.** Modules are strict mode, so
   `err.rollbackIncomplete = …` raises a TypeError on a string, frozen Error or null — replacing
   the real failure AND dropping the dirty-tree signal, which made the CLI report a clean
   rollback over a dirty tree. `specialMerge` is caller-supplied on an exported API, so this
   needs no brain-side bug to reach.
7. **A test suite can be green and still miss the dominant shape.** The first test round always
   left exactly ONE entry in `toCopy` — the one that throws — so plain-copy rollback was never
   exercised, despite 364 of 366 real managed files being plain copies. Every rolled-back write
   in the suite came from a merge fn. Fixed by sorting the write order and adding REQ-S6-10.
8. **`brain:review` at `tier: lite` resolves to `brain-review/1`**, which has no
   findings-producing evaluator: `findings: []` means "nobody looked", not "the code is clean".
   `/2` — the half that wires causal-admission and the refuter — is `regulated`-only. This is
   epic #313's #409 observed live, not a defect.
9. **The reviewer identity is declared, never proven.** `identity.mjs` returns
   `reviewerConfig.handle` and nothing cross-checks the token against it, so the §10 self-review
   abstention and the anti-loop lock are forgeable. Filed as #413; sibling of #382.
10. **`actor-check`'s `lite` evidence is a distinct ACT, not a state.** The approved-label event
    must be strictly later than the PR's head commit, so every push invalidates the previous
    approval. Working as designed — Q5's fix for the stale-green class — but it will read as a
    broken CI to anyone who has not seen it.

## Corrections made to my own earlier claims
- Reported `TIER_PARAMS.lite.diffBudget` and `.artefacts` as unconsumed "one rule, two
  implementations" divergences. **Both were wrong**: `diffBudget` is read by `brain-check.mjs`,
  `brain-audit.mjs` and `merge-walk.mjs`; `artefacts` by `phase-order-check.mjs`. `check-refs`
  demanding all four artefacts is a deliberately tier-independent STRUCTURAL check. The wrong
  conclusion came from a mutilated grep (`rg -r` consumed the pattern as a replacement string).

## Next steps
- **#396 slice 2 — the on-disk journal.** The M4 hard gate stays CLOSED until it lands. It must
  INVERT `createRestorePoint`'s entry-time clearing of a pre-existing snapshot: once recovery
  exists, a leftover snapshot is evidence to replay, not debris. Flagged inline.
- Human: re-apply `status:approved` on #396 after the last push; ratify or reject ADR-0027;
  Tier-2 promotions for #397, #405 and #414.
- Then #397/#398/#399, #401, #413, and M3 closure (#409 → #405 → #408).

## Relevant files
- `brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs` — `createRestorePoint`, `annotateRollback`, guarded write loop
- `brain/scripts/lib/installer.test.mjs` — REQ-S6-1..14
- `brain/scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs` — signal-before-status, rollback reporting, interrupt handling
- `docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md` — partial fix with all four residual gaps enumerated
- `openspec/changes/issue-396-upgrade-rollback/` — proposal, spec, design, tasks, ADR-0027 draft

**Session summary: brain — M4 upgrade safety (#396, #399, #398 closed; #397 designed and handed off)**

## Goal
Advance M4 — epic #313's HARD GATE, which blocks external adopters from upgrading
safely. Closed #396, #399 and #398; designed #397 and handed it off.

## Accomplished
- **#396 CLOSED** — restore point + on-disk journal + explicit `--recover` + an exclusive
  lock. ADR-0027 signed. Took EIGHT adversarial review rounds.
- **#399 CLOSED** — merge pre-flight + `--skip-merge <path>`; the corrupt-JSON lockout has
  an escape.
- **#398 CLOSED** — downgrade guard before the install, naming the config keys left ahead.
- **#397 DESIGNED, ratified, NOT implemented** — handed to a fresh agent.
- Spun off and closed by the maintainer: **#413** (reviewer identity now verified against
  the token) and **#418** (lite distinct-act re-arms only on FOREIGN commits — ADR-0026
  Amendment 1). Still open: **#414** (Tier-2), **#415** (cosmetic).

## Discoveries that cost the most to find
1. **A green suite proves nothing about a CLI it never runs.** Twice on #396 a fully green
   suite hid a broken product: once the feature did nothing (the `acquireLock` call site
   was deleted as collateral of a scripted edit), once `brain:upgrade` failed 100% of the
   time (the run read its own live lock as a competitor and refused itself). Both passed
   ~2290 tests. The fix was REQ-J-9 (the lock is HELD while it works) + REQ-J-10 (the
   upgrade completes and the bytes change). **Neither is sufficient alone.**
2. **A cleanup that judges locally will eventually delete something another site owns.**
   Four consecutive rounds produced that same shape, each introduced by the previous fix:
   a `finally` discarding the snapshot; a retry clearing the preserved copy; a catch
   destroying the evidence a refusal pointed at; `breakStaleLock` deleting a LIVE run's
   mutex. Resolved structurally with `inspectRestorePoint()` — ONE reader, ONE verdict
   (clean/debris/interrupted/corrupt/live-run) — and an ALLOW-list at the one remaining
   cleanup site.
3. **Signal handlers cannot interrupt a synchronous fs loop.** Measured: SIGINT at 40ms
   into a 935ms sync copy ran to completion, handler after. So registering a handler is
   not a mid-write abort — it stops the default action from killing the process, which is
   the only thing that half-applies a tree. Corollary, also measured: a run wedged on a
   hung managed path can then only be ended with SIGKILL.
4. **"Could not read it" is not "nobody owns it".** Widening lock reclaim to unowned locks
   accidentally widened it to UNREADABLE ones (EACCES/EIO/EMFILE/ESTALE), inverting the
   stated property from "it strands, it never permits" to permitting.
5. **schemaVersion has TWO writers with DIFFERENT meanings** — `ensureBrainConfig`
   (env:init) writes the newest MIGRATION version, `migrateConfig` writes the installed
   PACKAGE version, and migrations top out below the package. A downgrade guard trusting
   that field alone missed the six most recent of sixteen tags — the fresh-adopter
   population the gate exists for. Compare against the highest thing actually TRUE.
6. **AGENTS.md is GENERATED and its inputs straddle the ownership line.** `brain/HOME.md`
   matches neither `managed` nor `local`, so the consumer owns it. Plain-copying AGENTS.md
   therefore hands every consumer BRAIN's AGENTS.md, compiled from BRAIN's HOME.md — a file
   describing the wrong repository, in every consumer, from the first upgrade. This is the
   finding #397 does not contain and it reshaped the design.
7. **The collision check conflates two facts.** dest-vs-INCOMING answers "do these differ",
   not "did the consumer edit this". The missing third point is free: before the install,
   `node_modules/brain/<path>` is what brain shipped LAST time.

## Corrections I had to make to my own claims
- I wrote that #399 "strengthened" the #180 clobber guard. It WEAKENED it: I moved the
  assertion from the call site to the declaration, and mutating `specialMerge: mergeMap`
  to `{}` reproduced #180 with the whole suite green. Fixed with a behavioural test.
- I described reading the OUTGOING migration list as a tradeoff to apologise for. It is the
  only thing that works — a target's own list can never contain a migration above itself.
- Two "one rule, two implementations" divergences I reported (`diffBudget`, `artefacts`)
  were FALSE. Both params are consumed. The wrong conclusion came from `rg -rn`, where
  `-r` silently consumed the pattern as a replacement string.

## Method that worked, and should be kept
Measure the real behaviour before designing — three of the four M4 tickets had premises
that had already shifted. Write the test FIRST and prove it red. Drive the real CLI, not
the library API. Run one adversarial review per slice: the two I nearly skipped as "small
and safe" each found a real hole in the target population.

## Next steps
- **#397 implementation** — classification RATIFIED 04/08/2026, phases 2-4 unblocked,
  handed to a fresh agent. Tier-2 signature already obtained; do not re-litigate the table.
- **#401** — the danger-path e2e. **This is what makes the hard gate checkable**; three of
  its four paths now have real behaviour to assert, the fourth arrives with #397.
- **#400** — `npx brain init`, independent.
- **THE HARD GATE IS STILL CLOSED.** It opens when #401 is green, not when the fixes land.

## Relevant files
- brain/scripts/lib/installer.mjs — restore point, journal, recovery, lock, pre-flight, downgrade helpers
- brain/scripts/brain-upgrade.mjs — the CLI surface and every refusal path
- brain/scripts/lib/installer-journal.integration.test.mjs — REQ-J-*, REQ-M-*, REQ-D-* (all drive the real CLI)
- brain/project/decisions/adr-0027-upgrade-rollback-is-restorable-not-atomic.md
- openspec/changes/issue-397-clobber-asymmetry/ — the ratified design awaiting implementation

## Goal
Pick up the brain 1.1 line and advance M4 — the epic #313 hard gate that blocks external
adopters from upgrading safely. Owner chose M4 over M3 closure, then chose to deliver #396

## Accomplished
- **#396 slice 1 shipped to review** — PR #412 (draft), chain `main ← feature/issue-396-rollback

  write and restores those bytes on any throw; an incomplete rollback KEEPS its snapshot and
  reports where. Symlinked managed paths are refused up front. Suite 2268 → 2282.
- **Full SDD change dir written** at `openspec/changes/issue-396-upgrade-rollback/` —
  proposal, spec (REQ-396-1..9 with scenarios and negative controls), design, tasks, plus
  `brain-drafts/adr-0027-upgrade-rollback-is-restorable-not-atomic.md`.
- **Three follow-up issues filed**: #413, #414, #415. Epic #313 re-synced with a status block,
  a rewritten M4, and an explicit priority table for the next agent.

## Discoveries
1. **#396's stated exit criterion is unachievable as written.** `rename(2)` is atomic for ONE
   path; the managed payload spans four disjoint locations (`brain/**`, `.github/**`,
   `.gemini/**`, root files), so no single directory swap can commit it. Multi-file atomicity
   needs a journal. Restated as *restorability*, with each residual gap named — ADR-0027 draft,
   unsigned.
2. **A signal handler cannot interrupt a synchronous fs loop.** Measured: SIGINT at 40ms into a
   935ms sync copy loop → the loop ran to completion (i=60000) and the handler fired after;
   the same loop with a `setImmediate` yield aborted at i=2251. So registering a handler is not
   a mid-write abort — it suppresses the default terminate action, which is the only thing that
   genuinely half-applies a tree. The real managed write is 366 files in ~23ms.
3. **`spawnSync` returns `{status: null, signal}` when the child dies by signal.** A first
   revision claimed, as measured, that a Ctrl-C during `npm install` was caught by the deferred
   interrupt guard. It was not: `if (r.status !== 0)` fires first, reporting the interrupt as
   "install failed — check repo access" and collapsing exit 130 into 1. Registering the handler
   is what kept the parent alive to reach that branch, so the slice introduced that regression.
   Fixed by testing `r.signal` before `r.status`. Recorded rather than rewritten out of history.
4. **`existsSync` follows symlinks.** A dangling symlink at a managed path therefore read as
   absent, was recorded as created-by-this-run, and was DELETED on rollback — while
   `copyFileSync` wrote through the link to a target outside the repo, and the rollback reported
   success. The feature corrupting what it exists to protect. Presence must be judged with
   `lstat`.
5. **A `finally` is the wrong place to discard a restore point.** It runs after `catch`, so it
   deleted the snapshot on the incomplete-rollback path — the one branch where the snapshot is
   the only surviving copy of the consumer's bytes, and the same branch whose message tells the
   operator to go inspect them. Only a complete rollback may discard.
6. **Annotating a caught error can throw.** Modules are strict mode, so
   `err.rollbackIncomplete = …` raises a TypeError on a string, frozen Error or null — replacing
   the real failure AND dropping the dirty-tree signal, which made the CLI report a clean
   rollback over a dirty tree. `specialMerge` is caller-supplied on an exported API, so this
   needs no brain-side bug to reach.
7. **A test suite can be green and still miss the dominant shape.** The first test round always
   left exactly ONE entry in `toCopy` — the one that throws — so plain-copy rollback was never
   exercised, despite 364 of 366 real managed files being plain copies. Every rolled-back write
   in the suite came from a merge fn. Fixed by sorting the write order and adding REQ-S6-10.
8. **`brain:review` at `tier: lite` resolves to `brain-review/1`**, which has no
   findings-producing evaluator: `findings: []` means "nobody looked", not "the code is clean".
   `/2` — the half that wires causal-admission and the refuter — is `regulated`-only. This is
   epic #313's #409 observed live, not a defect.
9. **The reviewer identity is declared, never proven.** `identity.mjs` returns
   `reviewerConfig.handle` and nothing cross-checks the token against it, so the §10 self-review
   abstention and the anti-loop lock are forgeable. Filed as #413; sibling of #382.
10. **`actor-check`'s `lite` evidence is a distinct ACT, not a state.** The approved-label event
    must be strictly later than the PR's head commit, so every push invalidates the previous
    approval. Working as designed — Q5's fix for the stale-green class — but it will read as a
    broken CI to anyone who has not seen it.

**Amending an ADR is a three-step change — decision-gate and the AGENTS.md drift-guard both fire (brain, #418/#425)**

3. **The `AGENTS.md` drift-guard then fails.** `AGENTS.md` is COMPILED from 5 `SOURCE_DOCS` (`harness/backends/antigravity.mjs`), one of which is `brain/HOME.md`. Touching the index leaves the committed `AGENTS.md` byte-different from its sources. 1. Author records through `buildRecord()` + `validateRecord()` from `brain/scripts/memory/lib/format.mjs`. Pass `title` separately from `content`; `buildRecord` folds it into a bold Markdown prefix BEFORE hashing, which is what makes ids reproducible across machines.

`rebuildIndex: id mismatch at 2026-08.jsonl:2 — stored id '...' does not match the recomputed id '...' (tampered or stale record)`

- **`gh pr edit` is broken here** — fails with `GraphQL: Projects (classic) is being deprecated ... (repository.pullRequest.projectCards)` and applies NOTHING. Workaround: `jq -n --arg t "<title>" --rawfile b body.md '{title:$t,body:$b}' | gh api -X PATCH repos/csrinaldi/brain/pulls/<N> --input -`. Always verify with `gh pr view`.
- **`sd` is not installed** and invoking it triggers a sudo prompt that fails. Use the Edit tool for in-place source mutation.
- **brain's diff-size counter excludes `**/*.test.mjs`** via `governance.ignoreList`. Run `git diff --numstat <base> | node brain/scripts/vcs/diff-size-count.mjs` for the number the gate uses.
- **`npm run session:start` takes ~20 minutes**, blocked in `memory/cli.mjs import` (full re-import of 1722 records / 18 MB, no watermark), emitting nothing until done. Exit 0. → #433.

- **`strategyFor` must give exact literals priority over globs** — `brain/scripts/ci/gitlab-governance.yml` is REFUSE under the `brain/scripts/**` COPY glob.
- **Git history is unusable for clobber detection**: brain's own `AGENTS.md` changed 16 times across 17 tags, so a history rule fires for nearly every consumer — the exact thing REQ-397-6 Scenario 2 forbids. Measured, then rejected.
- **A negative control cannot be proven RED by deleting the feature.** With no detector, nothing fires, so it passes for the wrong reason. Prove it by MUTATION — removing the Scenario-2 gate failed exactly the two negative controls and nothing else.

2. **The #418 amendment silently required a guard nobody drafted.** Pre-amendment, "an unreadable approval is not an approval" was IMPLICIT: a missing label timestamp made `compareTimestamps` return null and the comparison fail. Amendment 1 adds a path (no foreign commit → satisfied) that never reaches that comparison, so a timestamp-less approval would have passed. Caught by an existing test, not by review — the invariant is now stated outright.

## Residuals still open
- **The `whoami` contract row is STALE.** `vcs-contract.md:26` still reads `() -> { username }` while shipped code accepts `token`. Replacement text sits in `openspec/changes/issue-413-reviewer-identity-verified/brain-drafts/`. Needs a Tier-2 promotion AND a new issue — #413 is closed, and every PR to `main` must close an open `status:approved` issue.
- **#418's relief does not reach the agent loop.** The exemption keys off the login the PROVIDER attributes to a commit, never the commit header (trusting the header would make the exemption forgeable in exactly the way #413 closed). Agent sessions committing as `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` resolve to no account ⇒ foreign ⇒ still re-arm. GitLab is in the same position wholesale (`prCommits` resolves no logins there). Closing it is operator-side: attribute session commits to an exempt account, or register a real bot identity.

## Test discipline applied (the epic's standing rule)
Every behavioural change verified RED against the pre-change code: 6 for #413, 5 for #418. In both PRs a control was deliberately kept GREEN on both old and new code and documented as such — #413's case-insensitivity check and #418's "third-party push still re-arms" / "unresolvable authorship is foreign". Those controls guard against an over-permissive fix, which a red-only suite cannot express.

## Process
Worktree per issue, branch names reproduced from `deriveBranchType` + the 40-char slug rule because `brain:ticket:start --worktree` fails without a VCS token in this container. Full suite run inside each worktree separately.

**Amending an ADR is a three-step change — decision-gate and the AGENTS.md drift-guard both fire (brain, #418/#425)**

Learned by hitting each step in sequence on PR #425, each surfacing only after the previous one landed. Nothing in the repo documented the chain.

1. **Edit the ADR** under `brain/project/decisions/`. `brain/**` is human-only (`consolidation-protocol.md` zone map: *"if the destination is brain/, the signature is human"*), so an agent drafts into `openspec/changes/{id}/brain-drafts/` and the human promotes.

2. **`decision-gate` then fails.** `checks/adr-presence.mjs` enforces an **unconditional** ADR ⇔ `brain/HOME.md` co-occurrence: touch one without the other and it refuses. It does NOT distinguish a new ADR from an amended one, so `HOME.md` must move even when it already indexes that ADR. Also human-only. In practice the gate was RIGHT — the index entry genuinely did not mention the amendment, and an index that misdescribes the document is what that gate exists to prevent. (ADR-0026's own Consequences section already recorded this check's divergence from its documentation as a known residual; it read as a footnote, not as an operational warning.)

3. **The `AGENTS.md` drift-guard then fails.** `AGENTS.md` is COMPILED from 5 `SOURCE_DOCS` (`harness/backends/antigravity.mjs`), one of which is `brain/HOME.md`. Touching the index leaves the committed `AGENTS.md` byte-different from its sources. Fix by REGENERATING — `AGENT_PLATFORM=antigravity node brain/scripts/harness/cli.mjs init` — never by hand-editing, which is precisely what the guard exists to catch. `AGENTS.md` lives at the repo root, not under `brain/`, and is a generated artifact, so an agent may regenerate it.

**Plan all three up front.** Doing only step 1 produces a red PR, and fixing that produces a second red PR. None of the three gates is misfiring — the chain is the real coupling between doctrine, its index, and the compiled artifact.

**How to capture memory when the engram binary is absent (brain, #410/#426)**

`memory:share` and `brain:save` both fail with `engram binary not found` in the Claude-Code-on-the-web container, so nothing is captured automatically and `git status -- .memory` stays clean. #410 established the workaround but recorded it **only in a PR body and commit message** — not in a memory record — so the next agent to capture a session would hit the same wall with nothing to warn them. This record closes that loop.

**The procedure:**
1. Author records through `buildRecord()` + `validateRecord()` from `brain/scripts/memory/lib/format.mjs`. Pass `title` separately from `content`; `buildRecord` folds it into a bold Markdown prefix BEFORE hashing, which is what makes ids reproducible across machines.
2. Append the serialized records to `.memory/records/YYYY-MM.jsonl`.
3. Run `npm run memory:reindex` — explicitly backend-agnostic (`memory/cli.mjs`: *"regenerate .memory/index.jsonl from .memory/records/ alone"*), so it works with no engram present.

**Never hand-write ids.** They are `"rec-" + sha256(canonicalJson(hashInput))[:16]` and `rebuildIndex` recomputes and verifies every one on each reindex. A first attempt using random ids was rejected outright:
`rebuildIndex: id mismatch at 2026-08.jsonl:2 — stored id '...' does not match the recomputed id '...' (tampered or stale record)`
That is the REQ-C4-1 id-equality check working. The store defends itself against invented content.

**Omit `issue` until #404 is fixed.** `computeRecordId` DOES hash the field when present, so the format supports it — but the transport drops it, so a populated `issue` would produce an id mismatch on the first engram round trip and poison the integrity check. Confirmed empirically: zero records across `2026-06/07/08.jsonl` carry the field, which is the "~0% adoption" #368 describes.

**A memory PR needs its own issue.** `governance.yml` requires every PR to `main` to carry `Closes|Fixes|Resolves #N` on a `status:approved` issue, and there is no exemption for memory. Historically memory rode inside work PRs; #410 and #426 each had to be filed purely to give a memory PR something legitimate to close. The pattern deserves a decision.

**Two silent traps: memory:share in a worktree, and a conflicting PR running ZERO checks**

**What**: Two failure modes hit while closing #397, both of which report success or look like something else entirely.

**1. `npm run memory:share` from a WORKTREE is a silent no-op.**
`.engram` is a symlink to `.memory` and is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:68`), so it does not exist in a freshly created worktree. The command then creates a REAL `.engram/` directory, exports chunks into it, prints `Created chunk <id> / Observations: N`, and materializes **nothing** into `.memory/records/`. `git status` stays clean.
- Symptom: share reports success, `git status` shows no changes.
- Fix: `rm -rf .engram && ln -s .memory .engram` in the worktree, or run it from the main worktree.
- Measured difference: bogus run reported 1 observation; correct run reported 1610 observations / 4 sessions / 16 mutations and appended 421 records to `2026-07.jsonl` + 10 to `2026-08.jsonl`.

**2. A PR with merge conflicts runs ZERO GitHub Actions checks.**
`governance.yml` triggers on `pull_request`, and GitHub cannot compute a merge commit for a conflicting PR — so no workflow runs at all. `gh pr checks` returns *"no checks reported on the branch"* and exits 1.
- This reads like a CI outage or a workflow-trigger misconfiguration, and sends you to inspect `on:` blocks. **Check `gh pr view <N> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` FIRST.** `CONFLICTING`/`DIRTY` is the real answer.
- Root cause of my instance: I ran the pre-flight merge verification, THEN added a commit (memory materialization) that touched `.memory/index.jsonl` — the file most likely to conflict. **Re-verify mergeability after any commit that lands after the merge check.**

**3. The correct resolution for a `.memory/index.jsonl` conflict** (the machinery #330 built):
`.memory/records/*.jsonl` carry `merge=union` in `.gitattributes` and auto-merge. `index.jsonl` is a **DERIVED projection**, not a source — never pick a side. Run `npm run memory:resolve-index`: it detects the conflict, regenerates the index from `records/`, and stages it (`✓ index conflict resolved — 2015 record(s) regenerated from records/ and staged`). Choosing a side on a derived file is how an index silently stops matching its records.

**Where**: `.gitignore:68`, `.gitattributes` (`/.memory/records/*.jsonl merge=union`), `brain/scripts/memory/cli.mjs` (`share`, `resolve-index`), `.github/workflows/governance.yml`.

**Learned**: both traps share a shape — the failure presents as success or as an unrelated problem. Verify the *effect* (`git status` after share; `mergeable` before blaming CI), never the *exit message*.

**#401: M4 danger-path e2e — local git remote, and the harness bug that made the clobber test vacuous**

**What**: Shipped #401 — the four M4 danger paths as a live e2e suite. Commit `c563345`, PR #441, all 9 checks green including the new `m4-danger-paths` job (1m26s in real CI). 21 assertions, 4 scenarios, zero product files touched.

**Where**: `test/upgrade/danger-paths.sh` (host runner), `test/upgrade/danger-paths-in-container.sh` (scenarios), `.github/workflows/m4-danger-paths.yml`, `package.json` (`test:danger-paths`), `test/upgrade/README.md`.

**Learned — the load-bearing findings:**

1. **The existing `run.sh` harness CANNOT test the REFUSE gate, structurally.** It does `npm i -D brain#TO` and THEN invokes `brain:upgrade`. Three-way detection (#397) reads the OUTGOING package *before* the install, so there `outgoing == incoming` → permanently degraded → the gate can never fire. The clobber scenario would have passed vacuously. If anyone extends `run.sh` for danger paths, this is the trap.

2. **`resolveInstallUrl` passes `git+file://` through unchanged** (its "unknown form, already prefixed" fallback branch, `installer.mjs:1483`). That is what lets a test build a bare git repo in-container and have `brain:upgrade` do its own REAL `npm i` against it — genuine install path, `outgoing != incoming`, and the suite tracks the BRANCH rather than published tags.

3. **npm installs from a local bare git repo carry `.github/**`** — verified by spike before writing the harness. brain has no `files` field in package.json and `private: true` does not block git installs.

4. **Mutation testing revealed message-vs-behaviour divergence twice:**
   - REFUSE gate removed → the run STILL printed "refused" and STILL exited 1, having written the files first. Every message-based assertion passed; only the byte-level check caught it.
   - Corrupt-JSON pre-flight removed → the file was STILL named and the run STILL stopped, from a later merge failure. The pre-flight's value is failing EARLY so `--skip-merge` works. Only behavioural assertions caught it.
   **Assert bytes and exit codes, not messages.**

5. **A new job in `governance.yml` is REJECTED by drift-guards** (`GOVERNANCE_JOBS`, `GATE_MATRIX`, job-order tests in `governance-checks.test.mjs` / `governance-tiers.mjs`). That job set is a ratified contract (ADR-0015) where every entry is a governance gate with a tier-resolved policy — and the file is a MANAGED path vendored to consumers. Maintainer-only CI belongs in its OWN workflow file, which is not managed and therefore never vendored.

6. **brain's own diff budget is 1000, not 400.** `brain.config.json` declares `tier: "lite"`, and `tierParams` maps lite→1000, standard→400, regulated→200. The PR template's 400 is the standard default.

7. **`docker run ... bash -s < script` silently does NOTHING without `-i`.** Exit 0, no output. Cost a debugging cycle.

8. **Scenario 1 deliberately departs from the ticket's "mid-upgrade kill"**: a real SIGKILL cannot be aimed inside a synchronous write batch. Deterministic equivalent that exercises the same restore-point machinery — TO ships a file under a new directory, the consumer has a FILE where that directory must go → `mkdirSync` throws ENOTDIR mid-loop after earlier writes landed.

**Next**: #441 awaiting merge. Once merged, epic #313's M4 hard gate is checkable — external adoption opens when this suite is green.

**engram import is ~0.6s per record — one execFileSync spawn each; blocks session:start and every git pull**

**What**: Measured the engram import on `main` with 1722 records / 18 MB:

| command | time |
|---|---|
| `memory/cli.mjs import` | **1053.30 s** (17.5 min) |
| `memory/cli.mjs resolve-index` | 0.13 s |

**0.61 seconds per record.**

**Why**: `backends/engram.mjs:542` — `importMemory` loops every record calling `_engramSave(...)` once each. `backends/engram.mjs:1017` — `_defaultEngramSave` is `execFileSync(engram, ["save", …])`. **One process spawn per observation.**

**Where it hurts — TWO triggers, same root cause:**
1. `session-start.mjs:274` (`step2HydrateEngram`) — spawns the import synchronously and blocks every later step. Prints nothing until done.
2. `brain/scripts/hooks/post-merge:30` — runs the same import after **every `git pull` or `git merge`**, with output redirected to `/dev/null`. Harder to diagnose: `git pull` just hangs with no signal, and the instinct is to blame the network, not a local hook. The `|| true` protects against failure, not duration.

**Learned — two SEPARABLE defects, easily conflated:**
- **No watermark** → re-imports all 1722 records every invocation (repeats finished work).
- **Per-record process spawn** → each record costs ~0.61 s regardless.

Fixing only the watermark is NOT enough: a perfect incremental import still pays ~0.6 s per *new* record, and a first-time import in a fresh clone — the adopter path M4 exists for — would still take 17 minutes. The load-bearing fix is a **batch/bulk save path** (one engram invocation for N observations, or a direct store write).

**Correction worth keeping**: `resolve-index` in the post-merge hook is technically redundant (git never fires `post-merge` on a failed merge, so there is never a conflict to resolve there) but costs **0.13 s** — it is NOT part of the problem. I initially framed it as if it mattered; it does not.

**Tracked**: issue #433, retitled to name the real root cause. Both triggers and the measurement are in a comment there.

**brain: nueve PRs, 62% → 92% del lazo operativo**

Nine PRs to main: the operational loop went 62% to 92%, and GitLab stopped being a separate number.

Landed (merge order): #506 rev-bound per head (PR 527) · #528 issueCreate + the port-level refusal that keeps the approval label human (531) · #459 brain:epic:map, dependencies as declared data (532) · #479+#475 the audit authenticates through VCS_TOKEN (534) · #480 the workflow-auth guard derives its rule from the invoked code (536) · #130 one rule, two pipelines (537) · #518 the audited set is the whole first-parent line (538) · #529 the memory-gate ruling (539).

Measure: 13 capabilities of the loop a user needs on a project X — 11 complete, 2 partial (#530 the writer, #533 who-is-executing), 0 absent. Both providers identical since #130.

Standing constraints: the agent never applies status:approved (#124); brain/** is Tier 2 so doctrine ships as a draft and the human's commit is the signature; issue-link on base main requires a closing keyword.

This record was written by `npm run memory:save` — the verb #530 makes reachable. Before it, nothing in this environment could write a durable record at all.

**#530: el escritor existía; faltaba alcanzarlo**

The capture path was UNREACHABLE, not missing.

Before: a records-only writer needing no engram EXISTS (plainfiles.mjs#save, fully tested) · not reachable by default (MEMORY_BACKEND defaults to engram) · no npm verb (index/share/pull/reindex existed, save did not) · `memory save "t" "c"` threw `canonicalJson: unsupported value type 'undefined'`, naming neither field nor flag · and engram's own refusal pointed at `engram save`, a binary `command -v` cannot find here.

A working writer existed and every signpost pointed elsewhere. Ruling (c), and smaller than the ticket assumed: reachability, not new machinery.

The asymmetry that is the fix: `project` is a FACT the config carries, so it is DERIVED (slug → name → directory). `type` is a CHOICE among seven, so it is REFUSED by name with the list. Defaulting type would stamp fabricated meaning onto a durable record. Derive facts, never opinions.

Why the crash had zero coverage: every existing plainfiles.save test passed BOTH fields. Green tests, unusable verb.

Found while guarding it: `t(key, params, { lang })` silently ignores the option — it is `locale`. My first reachability test looped en/es passing `lang` and asserted the SAME catalogue twice: N=1 wearing an N=2 loop. The guard now asserts the two strings DIFFER.

**#529: memory-gate es repo-scoped; el orden es la sustancia**

memory-gate is repo-scoped: ruling (1) now, sequenced to recency after the writer works.

Cost stated with the choice: the gate still cannot notice the next outage; what it buys is that nobody reads it as a per-change guarantee while it cannot be one. (2) recency lands after #530, and NOT before skip:memory-gate exists in code.

Why the order is the substance, measured: option (2) fails a PR whose base postdates the newest session_summary. The newest was 2026-08-04 and 34 merges had landed since — it would have blocked ALL of them. And the promised override does not exist: no code path checks skip:memory-gate. So (2) then would block with NO escape, and the only way out would be removing the gate.

Second defect found while measuring: the invariant table called row 3 "Hard with override". Neither half was true. The file already contradicted itself — the repo-global scope sat in the metrics caveats 120 lines BELOW the table, which is not where a reader forms the belief.

**#518: un tercio de main sin auditar**

A third of main was never audited, and the design question that held the fix made the model SIMPLER.

The walk selected `git log --first-parent --merges`. `--merges` means more than one parent, so a squash was never enumerated — not evaluated and passed: never looked at. Measured on origin/main over 60 days: 112 first-parent commits, 79 enumerated, 33 never audited (32 carrying a (#N) reference).

It compounded: a window with no findings exits 0, the cursor advances, and since the cursor only moves forward every unenumerated commit became PERMANENTLY un-re-auditable. No remediation path either — [FAIL-SHA] can only nominate a commit the audit enumerated.

The held question: every exemption predicate is built on `<sha>^1..<sha>` and nothing had decided what that means with no second parent. Answer: `^1` resolves for ANY non-root commit, and for a linear one it is simply its own diff — less ambiguous than a merge's contribution. So sign/netPresent/netAddFull/addedPathsAbsentAt needed NO change. Only the three ENUMERATORS moved, and together — widening one alone leaves the two sides disagreeing about what a window contains, worse than either narrow one.

Consequence: every commit on the integration line is now governed, including direct pushes. --first-parent untouched. Existing history is not re-audited.

**#479/#509: dos seams que parecían cerrados**

Two seams that looked closed and were not.

#479 — brain declares ONE neutral credential and nothing used it. getVcs() bound a credential only when a caller passed `identity`, and measured, exactly 1 of 20+ call sites does. The same audit authenticated two ways depending on provider with nothing asserting they agreed. Fix belongs in getVcs(), not threaded through the audit path.

The residual, visible only after removing the accident hiding it: ci-context.mjs imported prView STRAIGHT from providers/github.mjs, bypassing getVcs() and its credential resolution. It looked fine because every job needing the PR body also set GH_TOKEN, so gh authenticated by accident. Declaring VCS_TOKEN alone turned issue-link red.

#509 — promoting doctrine re-derives a written cascade every time. brain:promote handles the ADR shape only, so #529's methodology-doc ruling shipped as a bespoke script that missed regenerating AGENTS.md; CI caught it on the human's signing commit. brain:promote ALREADY does that. Two implementations of a written rule, one commit after it was written.

Trap: compileAgentsMd(docs) keys by relPath and falls back to `?? ''` per section — passing an ARRAY silently emits empty sections. It deleted 543 lines and returned successfully.

**Split paralelo: #530/#533 vs #535/#509/#435**

Parallel split, with the file overlap COMPUTED not asserted.

Agent A (this session): #530, #533. Agent B: #535, #509, #435.

Claims — #530: brain/scripts/memory/**, brain-save.mjs, session-start.mjs, .memory/**, package.json · #533: brain/scripts/vcs/providers/**, vcs/cli.mjs, brain/scripts/status/** · #535: .github/workflows/governance.yml, vcs/lib/workflow-auth.mjs · #509: brain-promote.mjs, harness/backends/** · #435: package.json, brain/project/decisions/**, docs/**.

Run through filesOverlap (the function #459 shipped): exactly ONE pair overlaps — #435 ↔ #530, both on package.json. Small and mergeable, but whoever lands second REBASES rather than resolving blind. The #522/#523 lesson: a conflict resolution silently deleted four tests, and deleting tests never turns a suite red.

#533's claim is deliberately narrow — vcs/providers/** and vcs/cli.mjs, NOT vcs/**. Claiming the tree would collide with #535 and serialise two tracks that need not be.

#535 needs status:approved before work starts; the agent may never apply it (#124).
